passage:
At the end of the hallway in our school, there is a small art room. For years, its door was always closed. Students passed by without looking inside.
This year, a new art teacher, Ms. Park, kept the door open after school. At first, no one entered. Then one student came in to borrow tape. Another came in to ask about a poster. Soon, students began staying to draw, paint, or simply sit quietly.
Ms. Park never forced anyone to make "good art." She put paper, pencils, and old magazines on the tables and let students choose what to do.
By winter, the art room became one of the busiest places after school. Some students went there because they loved drawing. Others went because it was peaceful.
Ms. Park said the room did not change much. The door did. Sometimes opening a door is enough to invite people in.
